confirmed.title: Sessione attiva con IP loopback 127.0.0.1/32 mostrata in ambiente di produzione
confirmed.evidence: Nel box 'Sessioni attive' una sessione e' identificata come '127.0.0.1/32' (indirizzo di loopback locale) con 'Visto l'ultima volta 22/06/2026, 21:41:49', accanto alla sessione reale '188.216.74.236/32' marcata 'Questo dispositivo'. Una sessione 127.0.0.1 e' un artefatto di accesso locale/dev visibile in produzione.
confirmed.note: Confermato leggendo lo screenshot D:/heuresys-advanced/audit/screenshots/clean-ess/me__security.png. Nel box "Sessioni attive" sono visibili due entry: (1) "188.216.74.236/32" con badge verde "Questo dispositivo", UA "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36", "Visto l'ultima volta 23/06/2026, 22:26:01"; (2) "127.0.0.1/32" con stessa UA, "Visto l'ultima volta 22/06/2026, 21:41:49", pulsante "Revoca". L'indirizzo 127.0.0.1 e' un loopback locale: in un ambiente prod dietro nginx reverse proxy (PROD HTTPS) una sessione utente reale dovrebbe portare l'IP client forward-ato, non loopback. Indica una probabile lacuna di trust-proxy / gestione X-Forwarded-For (coerente con il debito aperto D-28 TRUST_PROXY citato nella memoria di progetto) oppure una sessione residua da accesso locale/dev affiorata in produzione. Tutte le claim fattuali del finding (valore 127.0.0.1/32, coesistenza con la sessione reale 188.216.74.236/32 marcata "Questo dispositivo", timestamp 22/06/2026 21:41:49) sono verificate sullo screenshot. Severita': "low" appropriata e supportata (nessun segreto esposto, display read-only); "medium" sarebbe difendibile perche' il loopback segnala una mis-attribuzione IP sistemica delle sessioni in produzione, ma resta low.

confirmed.title: Org chart nodes are unlabeled dots — no position/unit identity visible

No data-correctness/crash/security issue — the 158 real positions and edges do render — so this is a presentation-layer readability failure, not a broken pipeline.

confirmed.title: Org chart edges are very low contrast against dark background

uncertain.title: Org-chart edges/connectors barely visible and many UUID nodes appear disconnected
uncertain.note:
Read the screenshot at 1.8x-4x zoom and measured edge contrast objectively. Split verdict on the two halves of the claim:

CONFIRMED half: the relationship curves ARE extremely faint. Isolating pure curve pixels (excluding bright node boxes) in the empty diagram region, the connector lines have luminance ~26 vs a background of ~16 — WCAG non-text contrast ~1.10:1 (max 1.19:1), far below the 3:1 threshold (WCAG 1.4.11). They are real thin curves, hard to read at normal viewing.

REFUTED half: the claim that the N_<uuid> column "has no clear connectors rendered to any parent" / nodes "appear disconnected" is wrong. At 4x zoom (gap between UUID column and labeled nodes) EVERY UUID node has a connector emerging from its right side, fanning into the parent position nodes (Securities Dealer, Risk Analyst), and arrowheads are visible where edges enter the labeled nodes. The hierarchy IS wired and traceable — the edges are just low-contrast, not missing.

So this is NOT a WIRING/data-connectivity defect (topology renders correctly: all nodes connected, arrowheads present). It is a visual/contrast legibility issue on the edge stroke color against the dark canvas. Type misclassified as WIRING. Severity lowered medium->low: cosmetic edge-contrast styling, no broken functionality or missing data. Marked verdict 'uncertain' because the headline mixes a true observation (faint edges) with a false conclusion (disconnected/unwired nodes) — the latter does not hold up to the screenshot.
